newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares hit seventh consecutive record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares hit seventh consecutive record.

text.p: Istanbul shares firmed in late buying fuelled by positive Treasury-bill auction results on Tuesday, but trade was quiet due to lower turnover, brokers said.

The IMKB-100 closed at a seventh consecutive all-time high of 92,797.71, up 663.50 points, or 0.72 percent from Monday's previous record of 92,134.21. Gains totalled 1.13 percent in the two days after last week's 5.49 percent surge.
Trade volume fell to 17.61 trillion lira from Monday's 18.54 trillion.
In dollar terms, the index was at $0.90, unchanged since Friday and compared to a record of $1 on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.

Brokers said the market was cautious earlier in the day due to uncertainty over the results of the Treasury's auction. The index sank to a low of 90,569 in an early selling wave before rebounding strongly in the morning session.
The Treasury sold 100 billion lira nominal-valued 273-day bills with Wednesday value, slashing the yield to 136.32 percent from 144.92 percent in the previous 182-day bill auction on November 19.
Banks will pay 51.5 trillion lira to the Treasury for the auction on Wednesday, in return for 164.5 trillion lira to be cashed in from maturing t-bills.
"Auction results were positive. The central bank will probably act tomorrow to drain surplus cash and keep the dollar's rise under control," said Murat Iman from Ata securities.

"The market may drift sideways for a while. Players switch to private sector shares from largely state-owned firms. Activity spills over to the whole market although volume falls which is healthy," he said.
Brokers said year-end profit prospects of companies began to fuel selective demand, but higher volume was needed for the market to advance towards its $1 index target.
Of the 230 shares traded, 87 advanced, 72 declined and 71 were stable. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.42 percent to 97,999.50 and the 15-share financial index rose 1.4 percent to 89,905.63.

Top actives were largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, down 750 lira at 13,750, Koc Holding, up 750 lira at 21,750 and leading car maker Tofas Turk Otomobil Fabrikasi, up 450 lira at 4,650. Together, they made up 31.9 percent of the total turnover.
